references.text: Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and horsemen followed the Israelites into the sea, as described in this earlier account of the pursuit.
The water returned and covered the Egyptian army, while the Israelites walked on dry ground through the middle of the sea.
The Lord divided the sea so that the people of Israel could walk through it on dry land.
Moses recalls how the Lord caused the waters of the Red Sea to flood over the Egyptian army as they pursued the Israelites.
The psalmist praises how the water covered their enemies, and not one of them was left.
God split the sea and led the people through it, while He let the water stand like a wall.
The prophet Isaiah refers to the Lord who brought out chariots and horses, and they lay there unable to rise again.
Hebrews mentions how the Israelites by faith passed through the Red Sea as on dry land, while the Egyptians drowned when they tried to do the same.
14:29 provides the visual detail of the miracle that 15:19 uses as a contrast to the enemy's downfall.
14:22 confirms the historical reality behind the theological summary in 15:19.
14:8 explains the theological cause (God's hardening) of the event summarized in 15:19.
14:28 describes the completed judgment that 15:19 celebrates as the Lord's decisive act.
14:27 explains the divine mechanism behind the event summarized in 15:19.
15:4 is a poetic parallel within the same text as 15:19, together forming a unified praise.
15:1 sets the theme for the entire song that 15:19 specifies and completes.
14:9 describes the critical situation before the entry that leads directly to the downfall in 15:19.
